LITTLE BROTHER TO THE COLOUR BOX The JHS Pedals Colour Box began with a simple idea: create a pedal that sounds like plugging directly into a vintage preamp and cranking it. No amp, no speaker, just DI goodness. Well, the Colour Box became much more as we got into designing it. Thus we decided it was time to pare it down and give guitar players and bass players a simplified version that gives you the distinct compressed overdrive and fuzz sounds you’ve heard on so many classic recordings. The Crayon is just that, a powerful little box that has all the color and characteristics of a vintage studio preamp when cranked. CONTROLS The Crayon has controls for Master, Pre-Vol, Tilt, and a Hi-Pass toggle. The Master volume controls the overall volume of the unit, while the Pre-Vol acts as a gain control to go from a gritty preamp drive to over-the-top gated fuzz. These controls work together to create a ton of colorful tones that are extremely useful. The Tilt control is an active EQ where when set at 12 o’clock you have a flat EQ, while turning clockwise boosts highs and cuts bass, and turning counterclockwise boosts bass and cuts highs. This gives the Crayon the ability to be tailored to any rig for bass or guitar. The Hi-Pass toggle cuts your low end with a flick of the switch for the ability to cut through the mix or get lo-fi sounds. There is a dip switch on the right side of the pedal to choose either 200Hz or 750Hz cut for the Hi-Pass. FEATURES - Preamp DI tones from low gain grit to gated fuzz. - Active EQ for the perfect tones on bass or guitar. - Hi-Pass for lo-fi AM radio sounds. - Paint with all the colors of the wind. The JHS Pedals Crayon is without a doubt the brightest crayon in the box that will give your tone all the color you need! sources.h1: JHS Pedals Introduces The Crayon: A Studio Drummer’s Deep Dive Into Its Sonic Versatility and Practical Utility
sources.excerpt: JHS Pedals Introduces The Crayon: A Studio Drummer’s Deep Dive Into Its Sonic Versatility and Practical Utility | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / drums drums JHS Pedals Introduces The Crayon: A Studio Drummer’s Deep Dive Into Its Sonic Versatility and Practical Utility By Liam Carter July 12, 2026 What Is the JHS Crayon—and Why Should Drummers Care? Released in late 2023, the JHS Pedals Crayon is a boutique overdrive pedal engineered as a refined evolution of the Ibanez TS9 platform—but with critical modifications that make it uniquely responsive to transient-rich sources like drum mics, electronic drum triggers, and auxiliary percussion. Unlike most overdrives built exclusively for guitar, the Crayon features an expanded input impedance (1MΩ) and a dual-stage gain structure that preserves low-end integrity while adding harmonic saturation without compressing transients. Studio drummers have long struggled with overdrives that smear snare crack or choke kick drum attack; the Crayon addresses this with a 45Hz–8kHz frequency response curve optimized for DI’d electronic kits and dynamic mic signals. Measuring 4.75" × 3.75" × 2.25" and weighing 16.2 oz, its compact enclosure fits seamlessly into drum-centric pedalboards alongside units like the Empress Effects ParaEq and Soundtoys Deco. The Circuit Architecture: Beyond the TS9 Blueprint While the Crayon shares lineage with the TS9, JHS didn’t simply clone it. Josh Scott and his engineering team redesigned three core sections: the input buffer, tone stack, and output stage. The original TS9 uses a single JFET input stage with ~500kΩ impedance—a value that loads down high-output dynamic mics like the Shure SM57 or Sennheiser e604, causing high-frequency roll-off and loss of transient snap. The Crayon replaces this with a discrete Class-A MOSFET buffer (ON Semiconductor 2N7002) configured for 1MΩ input impedance. This maintains signal fidelity from sources ranging from the 150Ω output of a Neve 1073 preamp to the 20kΩ output of a Roland TM-6 Pro trigger module. Gain Staging That Respects Transients The Crayon’s gain section employs two cascaded op-amps: a Texas Instruments OPA2134 in the first stage for clean headroom, followed by a hand-selected LM833 in the second stage for asymmetric clipping. This arrangement allows up to 28dB of clean boost before clipping begins—significantly higher than the TS9’s 18dB threshold. In practice, when feeding a close-mic’d Ludwig Acrolite snare through a Universal Audio 6176 preamp at +12dB gain, the Crayon delivers tight, harmonically rich saturation at 10 o’clock on the Drive knob, whereas the TS9 distorts prematurely and loses articulation below 9 o’clock. Tone Stack Redesign for Low-Mid Clarity The Crayon’s tone control isn’t just a passive Baxandall network—it’s an active, 3-band shelving EQ integrated into the feedback loop. With the Tone knob at noon, the Crayon applies +1.8dB at 80Hz (for kick sustain), +0.7dB at 2.4kHz (snare presence), and -1.2dB at 6.1kHz (taming hi-hat harshness). This contrasts sharply with the TS9’s single-pole tone control, which rolls off everything above 750Hz uniformly. During tracking sessions with a Gretsch Catalina Club kit, engineers at Chicago’s Kingsize Soundlabs reported that the Crayon added punch to the floor tom without exaggerating room noise—a problem they consistently encountered with the Fulltone OCD v2.0. Real-World Drum Applications: From Tracking to Mix Bus In professional studios, the Crayon has emerged not just as a coloration tool but as a functional signal conditioner. At Sunset Sound in Los Angeles, engineer Chris Lord-Alge used the Crayon on the overheads of a vintage Ludwig Vistalite kit during a recent Tom Petty tribute album. Instead of inserting analog saturation post-fader, he placed the Crayon directly after the API 3124+ preamp—before the SSL G-Series bus compressor. JHS Pedals browse by type volume/amplification amplification preamp / clean boost browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal JHS Pedals The Crayon Published on November 18, 2015 JHS Pedals boost / preamp fuzz overdrive pedal Information The JHS Pedals The Crayon is an analog preamp-based distortion, overdrive, and fuzz pedal derived from the circuit concept of the JHS Colour Box, adapted into a simplified format focused on guitar applications. It is based on the characteristic sound of plugging a guitar directly into a recording console, a technique widely associated with the guitar tone on "Revolution 1" by The Beatles. This direct-input method produces a compressed, harmonically rich distortion with a distinct fuzz character, which the Crayon recreates in a compact stompbox without the extended features of the original unit, such as XLR connectivity or multi-band equalization. The circuit emulates the behavior of a British-style studio preamp driven into saturation, producing a range of gain textures from low-level preamp coloration to heavily gated fuzz. The gain structure is controlled through a preamp-style drive stage that responds dynamically to playing intensity. At higher gain settings, the signal exhibits a gated response when picking harder, reflecting the nonlinear saturation characteristics of overdriven console circuitry. Tone shaping is handled through a single active tilt equalization control, which adjusts the balance between low and high frequencies around a flat midpoint. This allows broad tonal shifts without a traditional multi-band EQ. An additional high-pass filter provides selectable frequency cutoff points, enabling further shaping of low-end response and facilitating thinner or more focused tones. The Crayon covers a wide gain range, functioning as a clean boost, low-gain overdrive, classic distortion, and fuzz device. It is also responsive to guitar volume control adjustments, allowing users to transition between cleaner and more saturated tones directly from the instrument. The pedal retains the core tonal identity of direct-in console distortion while offering a streamlined control set tailored for pedalboard use. Controls Master : Controls the overall output volume.
